text:
I told the attending I wasn’t convinced.

Case 113. Drowning. The base excess number didn’t sit right with me, so I pushed back and asked for real data.

It pulled a 2015 review of 47 drowning cases. Mean lactate, 2.8. Mean base excess, negative 12.4. Then it walked me through why the deficit comes from the stress response, the hypoperfusion, the cold hitting the body all at once.

That is the moment it landed.

In a real hospital, you learn a tone before you ever open your mouth to your attending. Pushing back twice can feel like a risk to your standing in the room.

So what happens when that risk disappears?

You just ask. Again and again, until you actually understand it. No performance. No managing how it sounds.

The attending is not pulling from one person’s memory of one paper read years ago in residency. It is pulling from every case study, every review, all at once.

That is why we built it this way. The gap between not knowing and finding out should cost you nothing.
